strengths: can correctly locate 2/3 and 4/6 on a number line
verbally articulates that 2/3 and 4/6 are equal
uses visual diagrams to verify equivalent fractions
responds to diagrammatic scaffolding for proportional reasoning tasks
gaps: cross-multiplication for comparing 3/5 vs 4/7 is purely mechanical without conceptual explanation
cannot explain why cross-multiplication works for fraction comparison
failed first attempt on scaling recipe from 4 to 6 servings without scaffolding
no independent transfer on two novel context problems
learner_profile_summary.zone_of_proximal_development: transitioning from concrete-representational to abstract understanding of fraction equivalence and comparison; proportional reasoning emerging only with structured visual support

stage_diagnosis.current_substage: S4a — Consolidating Representational to Abstract Bridge
stage_diagnosis.rationale: Learner demonstrates reliable representational competence (number line, area/region diagrams) for equivalence but comparison reasoning remains procedure-bound. Cross-multiplication is executed correctly yet devoid of conceptual grounding, indicating a representational–abstract disconnect. Proportional reasoning is nascent and scaffold-dependent, with zero independent transfer to novel situations, confirming that generalized schema has not yet formed. S4 targets this specific representational-to-abstract transition before advancing to formal proportional reasoning.

learning_progression_position.prior_stage_mastered: S3 — Representational: uses number lines and diagrams to model and verify fraction equivalence
learning_progression_position.current_stage_target: S4 — Bridging to Abstract: builds conceptual explanations for procedures; transfers fraction reasoning to novel contexts with fading scaffolds
learning_progression_position.next_stage: S5 — Abstract/Fluency: independently compares, orders, and applies fractions in unfamiliar problems using flexible strategies

learning_objectives.description: Explain why cross-multiplication compares fractions by connecting it to equivalent fractions with common denominators
Compare any two fractions using at least two distinct strategies (benchmarking, common denominator, visual model) and justify the choice
Solve proportional reasoning problems (scaling, missing value) with fading visual scaffolds across at least two unfamiliar contexts
Generate self-explanations when solving fraction problems, transitioning from teacher-prompted to self-initiated verbal reasoning

instructional_strategy.approach: concrete-representational-abstract (CRA) bridge with structured fading and self-explanation prompts
core_techniques: dual-representation juxtaposition: present same problem in visual and symbolic forms side-by-side, then fade the visual
why-before-how questioning: require conceptual explanation before procedural execution on each comparison task
worked-example pairs with self-explanation: show correct and incorrect solutions, prompt learner to explain the error
graduated scaffolding: structured diagram → partial diagram → bare number sentence → novel context
strategy-comparison routines: solve same problem with multiple strategies and discuss which is more efficient and why

sequence.label: Expose the gap
activities: revisit 3/5 vs 4/7 comparison; use area models to show both fractions, derive common denominator 35 visually, then connect to cross-multiplication as a shortcut
learner writes or records a 'how it works' explanation of cross-multiplication in their own words, referencing the visual derivation

sequence.label: Build strategy repertoire
activities: compare fraction pairs using benchmarking (closer to 0, 1/2, or 1), common denominators, and cross-multiplication
for each pair, learner selects the most efficient strategy and justifies
introduce 'which strategy?' sorting tasks where learner matches fraction pairs to optimal comparison method

sequence.label: Scaffolded transfer — proportional reasoning
activities: recipe scaling with structured diagram: 4→6 servings, then 6→9, then 3→8
missing-value problems with fading diagrams: full strip diagram → partial → equation only
two novel context problems (different from diagnostic) with minimal scaffolding, emphasizing self-questioning prompts

sequence.label: Independent transfer check
activities: administer two new unseen context problems without any scaffolding
require written or verbal reasoning alongside each answer
compare performance to baseline diagnostic to confirm stage completion

recommended_resources.description: Fraction strip / bar model templates for common denominators and cross-multiplication derivation
Strategy-sorting cards: fraction pairs on one set, comparison strategies on another; learner matches and justifies
3 correct and 2 incorrect worked examples of proportional reasoning with prompts for self-explanation
Set of 6 novel context problems (mixture, rate, sharing) with graduated scaffolding levels

mastery_criteria.criterion: explains cross-multiplication in terms of equivalent fractions and common denominators without visual aid
compares fraction pairs using at least two strategies with correct justification for strategy choice
solves novel proportional reasoning problems independently (no diagram prompt)
produces unprompted self-explanations during problem solving
mastery_criteria.threshold: observed in at least 2 out of 3 sessions

progress_indicators.exit_gate: all four mastery criteria met → advance to S5; if transfer criterion not met after two instructional cycles → loop back to S4 phase 3 with intensified concrete-representational bridging and additional worked examples

estimated_duration.note: Pacing adjusts based on transfer checkpoint after phase 3; learners who clear the exit gate early may accelerate through phase 4
